headline: Town committees reviewed funding for a police drone program, advanced trail and wastewater planning, and released six subdivision lots.
synopsis: Southborough boards addressed several major capital and infrastructure initiatives this week. The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee endorsed a five-year police drone program while referring its year-end funding method to the Select Board for policy review. The Trails Committee finalized an estimated $450,000 application for a Peninsula Trail bridge, securing unanimous support from the Conservation Commission. Meanwhile, the Planning Board released six lots at the Ruby Estates subdivision, and the Wastewater Study Committee worked to secure consulting services ahead of a proposed fall sewer district vote.

highlights.title: Police drone proposal endorsed as capital priority
highlights.why: The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee voted to back a five-year, $105,000 police drone package as an immediate safety priority. Members deferred a decision on whether to fund the contract using surplus operating salary funds to the Select Board.

highlights.title: Peninsula Trail bridge plans advance with conservation backing
highlights.why: The Trails Committee finalized its Community Preservation Committee application for a footbridge connecting to the Fayville Dam, estimating costs between $440,000 and $450,000 after rerouting the trail to avoid a costly boardwalk. The Conservation Commission later voted unanimously to submit a formal letter supporting the funding bid.

highlights.title: Ruby Estates lots released and street tree study approved
highlights.why: The Planning Board accepted a surety agreement backed by a bond exceeding $300,000 and released six residential lots at 96 Mount Vickery Road. The board also voted to fund a $5,500 pilot study to identify 25 viable street tree planting locations near the town center.

highlights.title: Route 9 sewer district financing moves forward
highlights.why: The Wastewater Study Committee confirmed the town can designate a District Improvement Financing area boundary ahead of a full project plan, preparing for an October Special Town Meeting vote. Members worked to encumber up to $30,000 to hire MassDevelopment consultants to model commercial tax growth along Route 9.

highlights.title: Conservation Commission urges retaining longtime stewardship volunteer
highlights.why: Following the Select Board decision not to reappoint Freddie Gillespie to the Open Space Preservation Commission, the Conservation Commission voted to request that the Select Board convert her Stewardship Committee seat to an at-large position and reappoint her.
